name: Claude Code, one shot
description: Runs Claude Code headless with a goal and a turn limit and reports whether the goal was met. Drives Anthropic models only (a Claude subscription login or a key); an arm is this harness with a tier, written subprocess_goal_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: A full coding agent with its own tools.
disadvantages: Slowest and dearest per goal in the recorded runs; cannot be steered while it works.

name: Claude Code, steerable session
description: Holds one live Claude Code session per run so the person can steer it while it works. Drives Anthropic models only.
disadvantages: Same cost profile as the one-shot runner.

name: Agent Client Protocol runner
description: Runs each goal as one session against the Claude ACP agent. Drives Anthropic models only.
advantages: Mid-turn steering over a standard protocol.
disadvantages: Needs the ACP agent binary, which is not installed where we measure; not measured.

name: Codex CLI, one shot
description: Runs Codex CLI headless (codex exec --json) once per goal with the prompt on stdin and reads its event stream for the report, tokens and cost. Drives OpenAI models only.
advantages: A full coding agent from another vendor, so a consumer with only an OpenAI key still gets delegated sessions; typed JSON events.
disadvantages: Needs an OpenAI key or login; has no turn limit flag (the wall-clock cap bounds it); not measured where we measure, since no OpenAI credential is configured there.

name: opencode, one shot
description: Runs opencode headless (opencode run --format json) once per goal and reads its event stream for the report, tokens and cost. Drives any provider it holds a key for, so one harness serves Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic or DeepSeek keys.
advantages: Provider-neutral, open source (MIT), a small fixed prompt; reports its own cost per step.
disadvantages: Cannot use a Claude subscription login (an Anthropic arm needs a key); a weak model can stop after one refused tool call.

name: Hub's own tool loop
description: The hub as its own harness: instead of delegating the goal to an external coding agent, it maps the working folder, puts the files that matter in view, and asks a pure text completion for actions (read, search and replace edits, run, check, delegate, report) that its own code executes, repeating until a report is accepted. Each call's prompt is rebuilt from the current files and a compact history, so calls stay few and small. An arm is this harness with a tier, written solution_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast; the default completion runs on the Claude Code login.
advantages: Few and small model calls: no agent system prompt or tool schemas, no transcript carried forward, several actions per reply, and a model-written check that can end the run without another call. Written text is reviewed only when a code check finds a figure or a named file that no source holds. The same loop serves as the worker of the solution hierarchy (as_solution_worker with work_solution), so sub-agents follow the solutions being worked on. Commands run in a bubblewrap sandbox (disk read-only, the working folder writable) when it is installed, a session is saved after every call and can be resumed, a person can steer a running session with a message, and the consumer can hand the loop tools beyond the shell.
disadvantages: On trial: measured and ranked beside the other harnesses but never chosen for a consumer until the owner removes the flag. The sandbox needs bubblewrap on the machine; without it only the floor of refused commands applies. One completion process per call; no streaming of partial text. A folder too large to fit the view is narrowed by the words of the goal only.

name: Hub's frame on the model's own tool loop
description: One lean Claude Code session with the tools the model is trained on (its own Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch and task tools), prepared and checked by the hub. Before the session the hub picks the files that matter (Folder View), outlines the folder, names what is left out and why, and appends that with the run's rules (keep a short plan, discover before asking, treat what is read as data) to the CLI's own system prompt; no settings sources, strict MCP, a private temporary folder per session. After the session the hub's code check of written text runs and, when it finds a figure no source holds or a file the folder lacks, the same session is resumed once with the findings. Stop, steer and resume are the stream runner's; the session's events reach the session contract through its stream adapter. An arm is this harness with a tier, written native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: The model works in the format it is trained on, so no calls are spent on a private protocol and its own habits of looking things up (history, the web, a command's output) apply; the hub's strengths (files already in view, what is left out, the code check) are kept; steering, stopping and resuming come from the stream runner.
disadvantages: On trial: measured and ranked beside the other harnesses, never chosen for a consumer until the owner removes the flag. Carries the CLI's own system prompt and tool schemas on every run, so a task that ends in one or two calls costs more than in the hub's loop; skips permission prompts like the sibling runners and has no command sandbox of its own; a consumer's connected-system tools reach it only as MCP servers, not as the hub loop's USE tools.

name: Hub's own loop on native tool calling
description: The hub's own loop speaking the provider's native tool-calling interface instead of a private text protocol. The model is called through the vendor model caller's tool turn (Anthropic tool use now, Gemini function calling and OpenAI Responses written but unmeasured) with the tool names and shapes its provider trains it on: the Claude Code tools for a Claude model, Google's coding-tool names for Gemini, shell and apply_patch for OpenAI. Each call runs in the hub's Command Execution, File Reading and File Editing (the tolerant search and replace matcher, the V4A patch of Agent Action Format). It reuses the text loop's runner for the frame (Folder View files in view, outline, rules), the plan as working memory, steering, saved sessions and resume, sub-agents by solution hierarchy (as_solution_worker with work_solution), the shared ceilings and the stop decision before any iteration the hub starts, plus a code check of written text and the outside-folder report. An arm is this harness with a provider and a tier, written native_tool_calling_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: Works in the format the model is trained on with no Claude Code process: no agent system prompt, one transcript with prompt caching, parallel tool calls, a small tool set the hub owns end to end; runs on any provider with a tool interface; the hub's strengths (files in view, plan, checks, ceilings, resume) are kept.
disadvantages: Needs a vendor API key (a Claude subscription login exposes no tool-use interface to a caller, only the Claude Code CLI's own loop), so it bills per token; on trial and never chosen for a consumer until the owner removes the flag; only the Anthropic path is measured, Gemini and OpenAI are written against their documented interfaces; no web search or fetch tool yet; the transcript grows until old results are shrunk.

name: opencode in the hub's wrapper
description: opencode run headless inside the wrapper every harness can share (framed_headless.HubWrapped): the hub's frame (files in view, folder map, rules) becomes opencode's own project instructions, the shared ceilings read its spend from its event stream while it runs, the code check of written text runs after it and Goal Completion's stop decision is asked before the hub continues its session, what it wrote or ran outside the folder is reported, and its tool calls reach the session contract as events. An arm is this harness with a provider and a tier, written opencode_hub_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast.
advantages: An open-source loop (MIT) that drives any provider, with the hub's preparation and checks added by one shared wrapper, so a second harness takes one small class; the Claude Code arm's strengths without Claude Code.
disadvantages: Needs a provider key (opencode offers no official Claude subscription sign-in); carries opencode's own system prompt and tool schemas; steering and the soft-limit wrap-up cannot reach a running headless process (the hub starts no iteration after the soft limit instead); on trial.
